function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "is chrome is installed". They want to check if Chrome is installed. We need to use the tool to run a command. On Windows, we can check via registry or existence of path. Let's try to check typical installation paths: C:\Program Files (x86)\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe or C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe. We'll attempt to check existence. Use dir command? Or test file existence. We can use 'if exist' command. But we can't easily parse output. Maybe just run 'where chrome' which returns path if found. So let's call cmd_controller_execute with command: 'where chrome', unit: 'file'.

We should handle errors. If where fails, it will return error code. But we can capture output? The function returns whatever os.system returns. That might be exit status. But we don't get stdout. So maybe better to use 'dir /b /s "%ProgramFiles%\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" || dir /b /s "%ProgramFiles(x86)%\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe"'.

But again no output. Hmm. Since we cannot read output, we may rely on exit code. os.system returns exit status. So we can interpret non-zero as not found. So we can run 'where chrome >nul 2>&1' and then check exit code. But we can't see exit code either? Actually os.system returns exit status. So we can interpret returned value. So we can do:

result = cmd_controller_execute(command='where chrome >nul 2>&1', unit='exit_code'). Then result will be exit status. If zero, found; else not found.

Let's do that.
